title: Faith principles are not self-evident like science, yet we believe them immediately by the Spirit
source_text: V. In hoc quidem differunt principia fidei, et principia scientiarum, quod principia scientiarum per se nota sunt et evidentia, et sua luce cogunt intellectum ad assensum: principia vero fidei, quamvis moralem aliquam evidentiam habeant, tamen, logice et proprie loquendo, sunt inevidentia, neque sua luce assensum, qualem fides requirit, impetrant. Attamen in hoc conveniunt quod sicut principiis naturalibus assentimur immediate, per naturale lumen intellectus: ita quoque fidei principiis immediate credimus, per illuminationem et impulsum Spiritus sancti. Verum ut nihil obstat quominus aliquando principia naturalia probentur a posteriori: sic etiam fidei principia probari quidem possunt, sed a posteriori, et ad hominem tantum.
pass_a_gloss: In this indeed the principles of faith and the principles of the sciences differ, that the principles of the sciences are known through themselves and evident, and by their own light compel the intellect to assent: but the principles of faith, although they have some moral evidence, yet, speaking logically and properly, are inevident, and do not by their own light obtain the assent such as faith requires. Yet in this they agree, that just as we assent to natural principles immediately, through the natural light of the intellect: so also we believe the principles of faith immediately, through the illumination and impulse of the Holy Spirit. But as nothing hinders that sometimes natural principles be proved a posteriori: so also the principles of faith can indeed be proved, but a posteriori, and only ad hominem.
pass_b_english: Faith's principles and the sciences' differ here: the sciences' principles are self-known and evident, and by their own light compel the intellect to assent. Faith's principles, though they have some moral evidence, are — strictly and properly — inevident, and do not by their own light win the assent faith requires.

Yet they agree in this: as we assent to natural principles immediately by the natural light of the intellect, so we believe faith's principles immediately by the Spirit's illumination and impulse. And as nothing stops natural principles from sometimes being proved a posteriori, so faith's principles can be proved — but only a posteriori, and only ad hominem.
